source(here::here("chapters", "_setup.R"))
```

```

`r if (has_data) sprintf("All %d patients in the file are described here, in the arm they were randomized to: %d sugar water and %d licorice.", results$n_patients, results$n_by_arm[["Sugar water"]], results$n_by_arm[["Licorice"]]) else ""`
Baseline data are complete. Continuous variables are shown as mean (SD)
and categorical variables as n (%).

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: !expr has_data
#| tbl-cap: "Baseline characteristics by randomized arm."
labels <- c(
  age = "Age (years)", sex = "Sex", bmi = "Body mass index (kg/m²)",
  asa = "ASA physical status", mallampati = "Mallampati class",
  smoking = "Smoking", preop_sore_throat = "Sore throat before surgery",
  surgery_size = "Surgery size"
)
t1 <- results$baseline
t1$variable <- ifelse(duplicated(t1$variable), "", labels[t1$variable])
knitr::kable(t1, col.names = c("", "", "Sugar water", "Licorice"))
```

The arms are similar at baseline. Any differences between randomized arms
are due to chance, so there are no significance tests here, and nothing
in this table was used to choose covariates for the adjusted analysis.
Those were fixed in the plan (Chapter 3; D-009), for the reason given in
Chapter 4.

Two baseline facts matter for the pre-specified analyses:

- `r if (has_data) sprintf("Only %d patients had a sore throat before surgery.", results$preop_sore_throat_n) else ""`
  That is fewer than ten, so by the plan's rule this variable is left out
  of the adjusted model (D-011). The primary analysis keeps these patients
  (D-005).
- No other covariate in the adjusted model has a category with fewer than
  ten patients, so no categories are merged (D-016). Mallampati class has
  a very small top category, but it is not in any model (D-016).

No models are fitted in this chapter.
